title: Kibaku people — Grokipedia
text: December 25, 2025 - In December 2024, the Kibaku people organized their first cultural festival in over a decade in Chibok, reviving traditional dances, music, and communal displays disrupted by insurgency trauma since the 2014 abductions.[41] The event, attended by local leaders and residents, featured heritage exhibitions and local delicacies, serving as a deliberate assertion of cultural continuity and psychological resilience amid ongoing displacement affecting thousands in the region.[42] Organizers emphasized reclaiming pre-insurgency traditions to foster unity, explicitly framing the festival as a counter to Boko Haram's ideological erosion of local identity.
